name: The Garage
description: Six bays of polished concrete. Five cars under dust sheets, and one empty space with an oil drip in the middle.
arrival: The empty bay has been swept. At the back, a tack room with the alarm panel on the wall.

spots.label: Take the uniformed officer’s theft report
spots.text: The chauffeur found the roadster's bay empty at seven. Doors locked, alarm armed.

spots.label: Read the alarm panel's printout
spots.text: Saturday 23:00, armed. Sunday 02:04, disarmed, code 3. 02:30, re-armed, code 3. 07:02, disarmed, code 3.

spots.label: Examine the empty bay and the drive
spots.text: No soot on the wall behind the bay, where the exhaust would have been. Scuffs on the gravel all the way down the drive. It was pushed, not driven.

spots.label: Knock on the neighbour's door across the lane
spots.text: Mrs Albury, who doesn't sleep: 'A big grey Bentley sat on the lane with its engine running from quarter to twelve for ten minutes. Then it went.'

name: Hale House
description: A Victorian pile full of motor-racing trophies. The old man stays upstairs; his son has the run of the drawing room.
arrival: Oliver Hale is in the drawing room with a gin he poured before lunch. He raises it to you.

spots.label: Look at the letters on Oliver's desk
spots.text: A letter from the Regency Club: 'outstanding balance of £22,000 ... within fourteen days'.

spots.label: Ask to see Augustus Hale
spots.text: The housekeeper shakes her head. Mr Hale is in bed with his heart and seeing no one. That took longer than it should have.

name: The Coach-House Flat
description: Two neat rooms over the old coach house, with a window onto the garage doors and the lane.
arrival: Tommy Reece puts the kettle on before you've finished knocking. The flat is spotless. So are his shoes.

spots.label: Check the waste-paper basket
spots.text: Torn betting slips from a bookmaker on Mill Lane, and a final demand: £9,000.

spots.label: Go through the bureau
spots.text: Under the road atlas, a letter from Rotterdam in careful English: 'We can take a 1961 Castellane Sprint, no papers required, on delivery.' Addressed to T.R.

spots.label: Look out of the window
spots.text: A clear view of the garage doors and the lane. Anyone awake in here would have seen everything.

name: Ferri's Workshop
description: A lift, a paint booth, and a board of keys on hooks by the office door.
arrival: Marco Ferri slides out from under a Bentley on a creeper and wipes his hands on a rag that makes them dirtier.

spots.label: Check the key board
spots.text: The roadster's spare key hangs on hook 12. The sign-out card: 'Sat 17:00 O.H. — back 19:30.'

spots.label: Read the roadster's service book
spots.text: Thursday: 'Handbrake cable adjusted — releases fully now, car will roll on the slope. T. Reece informed.'

name: Kingsway Transport Yard
description: Car transporters in a row, a dispatcher's hut, and a clipboard of job sheets.
arrival: The dispatcher looks at your warrant card for a long time before he lets you into the hut.

spots.label: Go through the week's job sheets
spots.text: Job 6612, booked by telephone Wednesday: 'Night pickup Sun 02:20, Ashgrove Lane. One classic roadster, drive-on. Cash. Contact: T. Reece.'

spots.label: Talk to the night driver
spots.text: 'The bloke who rolled it on was the chauffeur from the big house. Uniform trousers, pullover over the top. He pushed it down the drive himself.'

spots.label: Look over the transporters
spots.text: Eight lorries, all empty, all washed. Whatever they carried last night is long gone.

name: The Royal Motor Club
description: Leather armchairs, framed Grand Prix posters, and a night porter who has seen everything and says nothing.
arrival: Philippa Crowe is reading the racing pages at the bar. Across the room, Desmond Pryce pretends he hasn't seen you come in.

spots.label: Ask the night porter about Saturday
spots.text: The porter's book: 'Mr Pryce returned 00:20, retired to his room. Breakfast 08:00.'

spots.label: Ask Philippa Crowe for her valuation file
spots.text: Her report from Tuesday, including a security note: 'Alarm codes held by the owner and the chauffeur only. Recommend a second code holder.'
